THE PROBLEM

A forwarded voice note can't take it back.

Schools send notices into parent group chats. When a time changes, the correction travels slower than the original, and an audio file that is already on someone's phone can never be updated.

Record it again and send it again.
The old recording keeps getting forwarded.
Nobody can tell which version is current.
In May 2026, Lagos State's Office of Education Quality Assurance publicly told schools to disregard a circulating message claiming students would be dismissed early the next day.
Source: OEQA Lagos, “Urgent Notice: Disregard Circulating Message on School Dismissal”. A real example of why corrections matter. It does not show that audio would have prevented it, and AfterSend is not affiliated with OEQA.

THE FIX

Fix the words. The link keeps working.

Edit the announcement and the new spoken version is prepared for you. Until you approve it, the link keeps playing the previous version. Once you do, the same link opens the corrected announcement for anyone who opens it next, with the full text beside the audio.

People who already have the page open are asked to reload it, so the audio never changes while they listen. Each version keeps its own text and audio, so a page never pairs old audio with new words.

HOW IT WORKS

Write, listen, share.
1
Write it

Type or paste the announcement. Dates, times and phone numbers are picked out so you can check each one before anyone hears it.

2
Hear it

AssemblyAI's text-to-speech prepares the spoken version when you stop typing, and again after every edit. You pick a synthetic voice. Nothing is public yet.

3
Share one link

Listen to the whole preview, publish, and share the link wherever families already are. That link stays the same for good.

TRUST AND LIMITS

What AfterSend will not do.

A correction tool is only useful if you can trust its limits.

Recall files
Downloaded or forwarded audio stays as it is. Only the link updates.
Verify publishers
AfterSend does not check who a publisher is. There are no verified badges.
Check facts
Speech reads the approved text. Making sure it is correct is the publisher's job.
Publish on its own
Every first announcement and every correction needs a person to approve it.
Clone voices
Only stock synthetic narrator voices. Never a real person's voice.
Send messages
AfterSend gives you a link. You decide where to share it.
